mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in real GDP growth, as measured by the quarterly GDP series (GDPC1), indicates strengthening economic fundamentals that support higher corporate earnings and positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth is positive (as measured by the latest quarterly report).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.3% from the prior month signals accelerating inflation, which triggers a shift in monetary policy expectations toward tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL rises >0.3% MoM, SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 45% of cases over the next 5 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and an increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a tightening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining UNRATE and rising PAYEMS fails to produce positive 60-day SPX returns in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of active monetary policy tightening (FEDFUNDS > 1.0%), an increase in the federal funds rate signals a contractionary stance that reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 1.0%, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1.1 million units per month indicates robust residential construction activity, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion and positive equity returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST is above 1.1 million.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 4.8% signals a strong labor market, which is associated with rising consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE < 4.8%, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 45% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer and housing demand, which drives corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising RSAFS and HOUST fails to produce positive 20-day SPX returns in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle economic expansion (GDPC1 growth > 2.0% annualized), a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals an overheating labor market that may prompt central bank intervention, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases when GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized and UNRATE declines.
